elements.evidence: "PB may terminate this Agreement at any time for convenience, in whole or in part"

elements.element: Customer convenience notice period of 60–90 days
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" — 30 days is below the 60–90 day fallback band (and is a preferred-only figure)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination" plus continuing "Approval Payments" — far exceeds any 3-month cap

elements.element: Vendor (SFJ) convenience termination permitted only effective at the end of a term
elements.evidence: 14.2.6 "SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control"; 14.2.10 "terminate ... at any time prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval" — no end-of-term limitation added
Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 contain no notice period for SFJ's termination right

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "at any time for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic; instead PB must pay "one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: 14.2.10 "SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval" remains untouched

reasons: Locked target was fallback, but the edit imports the preferred 30-day notice figure while leaving the fallback's 60–90 day band unmet; levels cannot be mixed.
No cap on the exit payment: PB still owes 100% of Development Costs plus future Approval Payments, well beyond the fallback's 'not exceeding 3 months' fees' limit.
SFJ's discretionary termination rights in 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 were not limited to the end of the then-current term and carry no 90 days' notice requirement, so both Vendor-side fallback elements fail.
Minimality fails: 'in whole or in part' adds new partial-termination scope not required by either level, and the notice figure was set at a preferred-only number rather than the fallback band.
Intent is preserved in the mechanical sense — the surviving Approval Payment and Trial Data Package mechanics still operate and no undefined term is introduced.
